answer: The costly-identity gate is the mechanism: each agent identity is backed by a stake slashed if it proves to be one of many sock puppets, and entry is priced so high that splitting one wallet into many identities costs more than acting honestly. Payout is capped per identity, but the slash hits the whole cluster found by shared funding trails, so a farm pays full stake per fake persona and forfeits all on detection, pushing expected profit to a nadir under honest yield. Funding graphs also expose the onyx of reused seed wallets, lifting marginal cost until the mesa of fakes flattens.
